title: Revolutions of 1848
summary: In the first half of 1848 revolutions swept Europe: they began in Palermo in January, toppled the French monarchy after barricade fighting in Paris on 22-24 February, and spread to Italy, the German states and the Austrian Empire, touching about 50 countries. Rulers granted constitutions and political freedoms, and serfdom was abolished in the Austrian Empire. Workers' risings were crushed, most bloodily in Paris in June, and by 1849 counter-revolution had restored the old regimes and left national unification and Polish liberation undone.

uncertainty.note: Main revolutionary wave concentrated in 1848–1849; isolated aftermaths in France and Germany persisted into 1851.

as_recorded.value: The revolutionary years of 1848 and 1989 stand out in modern history
1848 revolts were far more widespread than those of 1989, seriously affecting, if one counts all of the then-separate lands of Germany and Italy, about 50 countries in almost all corners of Europe
The 1848 revolutions occurred in lands from the Atlantic to Ukraine, and from the Baltic to the Black Sea
waves of revolution in modern European history—1789 to 1799, 1848 to 1851

where.modern_name: Paris, France (proxy epicenter; the revolutionary wave swept across continental Europe)

importance.justification: Europe-wide revolutions that ended serfdom in the Austrian lands and spread constitutional and national demands (R3 D2 T2 L3).

audience_note: Mentions the killing of thousands in the suppression of uprisings.

related.because: The July Monarchy established in France in 1830 fell in February 1848, triggering revolutionary unrest across Europe.
